description: Registered calls admit one schema-lifecycle job and return its job_id/status before declaration parsing or lifecycle effects. Destructive — drops every platform-owned table for the namespace and deletes the ownership rows. Refuses against an active namespace unless force=True is passed. Refuses to touch any table not recorded in ownership for this namespace.
embedding_description: Queue the complete schema lifecycle operation and read its exact job for the final outcome. Permanently drop all tables and ownership rows for a plugin namespace. Safe-by-default: refuses against active namespaces unless force=True. After uninstall_plugin_schema marks a namespace inactive, purge is the verb that actually removes the data.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Queued ActionResult receipt with data.job_id and data.status; the exact job.result retains the complete original lifecycle response and job.error its typed failure.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Admission confirms the job was persisted, not that the schema changed. Read service_interface::job_service::get_job by this exact id until terminal before using lifecycle status, tables or force results.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Poll the exact job id. Preserve the existing force and ownership premises. Reconcile an uncertain outcome or lost volatile declaration without replaying schema effects.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Drops platform-owned tables and ownership rows for the namespace in one transaction.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValueError: namespace is active and force=False. Postgres errors propagate from the transactional apply (failure rolls back atomically — no partial drop).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For 'refused — active': call uninstall_plugin_schema first to mark the namespace inactive, then call purge again. Or pass force=True if the data loss is intentional. For Postgres errors: confirm postgres_state_management_plugin is healthy; the transaction rolled back, no tables were dropped.
